newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Sweden repo rate cut to 4.10 pct Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sweden repo rate cut to 4.10 pct Tuesday.

text.p: The Riksbank is expected to lower its key repo rate by 25 basis points to 4.10 percent at its regular weekly tender on Tuesday, a Reuter poll of 14 economists showed on Monday.
Nine economists forecast a cut of 25 basis points from the current level of 4.35 percent, two a lowering of 20 basis points and one a 35 basis point cut.
One of the economists questioned forecast a cut of somewhere between 25 to 35 basis points and another forecast a cut of between 15 to 25 basis points.
The repo, which is the central rate in a three tier system, is the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity.

The economists questioned said the fact Sweden had showed a negative inflation trend for the past 12 months for two consecutive months was positive for another cut, which would be the 25th this year. The repo rate started 1996 at 8.91 percent.
The repo operation announced on Tuesday will run for three weeks to cover the holiday period which is another reason economists forecast a drop as large as of 25 basis points.
"It would be indefensible not to cut now. There is no sign of inflation and there is a three week repo so there will not be another until the middle of January," said one economist.
On the last two occasions the Riksbank lowered the repo rate, it has cut the rate by 25 basis points. The most recent cut was on November 26.
The repo operation will be announced at 0830 GMT on Tuesday.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from AGA, AMF Pension, Aragon, Carnegie, Consensus, Electrolux, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Midland, Nordbanken, Posten, S-E-Banken, Skandia, Stora, and Transferator.
